name: Cable Seated Row
summary: A seated horizontal cable pull targeting the latissimus dorsi, middle back, and biceps.

setup: Attach a close-grip V-handle to the low pulley of a seated cable row station.
Sit upright with your feet firmly braced on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
Grasp the handle with both hands, slide your hips back slightly, and establish a tall, braced torso perpendicular to the floor.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows backward tight along your ribcage.
Continue pulling until the handle touches your lower abdomen, squeezing your back musculature hard.
Pause briefly at peak contraction without leaning backward.
Slowly extend your arms and allow your shoulder blades to protract under control to return the weight stack without rounding your lower back.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handle toward your abdomen, and inhale as you return the weight under control.
cues: Drive your elbows into your pockets.
Squeeze your shoulder blades behind you.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso swinging to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Keep your torso nearly upright and stationary, initiating the movement with the back muscles rather than hip extension.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Depress your scapulae and keep your traps relaxed away from your ears.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lumbar spine at the front of the movement.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a neutral spine and soft bend in the knees; allow only the shoulder blades to protract forward.

precautions: Avoid using excessive body momentum that places sudden shear forces on the lumbar spine.
Never lock the knees out completely when braced against the footplates.
